title: Connect your AI assistant to FRED
gist: The St. Louis Fed launched an MCP connector letting AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT query FRED directly for data, metadata, transformed observations, downloads and FRED charts, positioning official data as the grounded source for AI-generated macro answers.

insights.claim: FRED now offers a connector built on the model context protocol (MCP), an open standard, so AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT can query FRED's economic data repository directly.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Official macro data is becoming a first-class, machine-readable input to AI assistants; expect AI-driven macro analysis to cite FRED series.

insights.claim: The connector exposes five tools: searching for data, inspecting metadata and methodology notes, retrieving observations with date ranges and transformations, generating CSV or JSON download links, and rendering FRED graphs linked back to fred.stlouisfed.org.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Covers the full workflow from discovery to charting, so analysts can automate routine macro lookups.

insights.claim: The St. Louis Fed frames the connector as grounding AI answers in the same trusted source used since 1991, claiming data integrity and accessibility commitments are unchanged.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Primary-source grounding is the pitch against hallucinated economic statistics in AI answers.
insights.quote: feel confident the source of that data is the same trusted source people have been using since 1991

insights.claim: FRED says it is being enhanced to match the way people now search for answers to data questions, signaling a shift from manual site browsing toward conversational AI as an access channel for official statistics.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Distribution of government data is moving into AI interfaces; data providers that don't expose connectors risk being less cited.

insights.claim: The connector can apply transformations such as converting an index level into year-over-year change, so an AI assistant can answer questions like year-over-year consumer price inflation with the actual series.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Reduces transformation errors in AI-generated inflation and unemployment answers; verify the series chosen.
insights.locator: What is year-over-year consumer price inflation?

insights.claim: Example use cases include comparing mortgage rates with the 10-year Treasury yield on a single rendered FRED graph and tracking how unemployment changed since the start of the year.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Shows the intended quick-look macro workflows an investor can now delegate to an assistant.
insights.locator: Compare mortgage rates with the 10-year Treasury yield.
